sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedatthi.

sentences.en: In June 2011, the Stanley Cup finals were underway in Vancouver.
sentences.zh: 2011年6月，斯坦利杯总决赛正在温哥华进行。

sentences.en: The city's beloved home hockey team, the Canucks, were playing against the Boston Bruins.
sentences.zh: 这座城市备受喜爱的本土冰球队——加人队，正在对阵波士顿棕熊队。

sentences.en: It was Game 7.
sentences.zh: 那是第七场生死战。

sentences.en: The team that won would take home the Cup.
sentences.zh: 获胜的球队将捧走奖杯。

sentences.en: In the last seconds of the game, Tim Thomas of the Bruins defended the goal and secured the championship for Boston.
sentences.zh: 在比赛的最后几秒，棕熊队的蒂姆·托马斯成功守住球门，为波士顿锁定了总冠军。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, crowds began forming outside of the stadium in downtown Vancouver.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，温哥华市中心体育馆外开始聚集人群。

sentences.en: They were upset.
sentences.zh: 他们情绪低落。

sentences.en: Just a few blocks from the stadium, fans decked out in Canucks jerseys began destroying the city.
sentences.zh: 就在距离体育馆几个街区的地方，身穿加人队球衣的球迷开始破坏这座城市。

sentences.en: They smashed windows and looted local businesses.
sentences.zh: 他们砸碎窗户，抢劫当地商铺。

sentences.en: Cars were overturned and set on fire.
sentences.zh: 汽车被掀翻并放火焚烧。

sentences.en: Jim Chu was police chief at the time.
sentences.zh: 吉姆·朱当时是警察局长。

sentences.en: He was working crowd control just blocks away from the center of the chaos that day.
sentences.zh: 那天，他在距离混乱中心仅几个街区的地方负责维持人群秩序。

sentences.en: Ten years later, he reflected on what happened that evening.
sentences.zh: 十年后，他回想起了那天晚上的情景。

sentences.en: It's hard to explain what happens when people get into a crowd mentality.
sentences.zh: 当人们陷入群体心态时，很难解释会发生什么。

sentences.en: And some of these rioters told us, I got caught up in the moment.
sentences.zh: 其中一些暴徒告诉我们：“我当时被气氛冲昏了头脑。”

sentences.en: One of the reasons I want to talk about this is...
sentences.zh: 我想谈论这个的原因之一是……

sentences.en: What could lead people to wreak havoc on their own city?
sentences.zh: 是什么导致人们对自己的城市大肆破坏？

sentences.en: How could ordinary fans so easily turn into violent rioters?
sentences.zh: 普通球迷怎么会如此轻易地变成暴力暴徒？

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, the psychological transformation that overcomes people
sentences.zh: 本周的“隐藏的大脑”将探讨当人们成为群体的一部分时，

sentences.en: when they become part of a group.
sentences.zh: 那种压倒他们的心理转变。

sentences.en: You have certainly had moments in your life when you were swept up by the fervor of the people
sentences.zh: 你的生活中肯定也有过这样的时刻：你被周围人群的狂热情绪卷入其中。

sentences.en: around you.
sentences.zh: 周围的人。

sentences.en: Maybe you broke into dance for the first time at a boisterous party and forgot your inhibitions.
sentences.zh: 也许你在一个喧闹的派对上生平第一次跳起舞来，抛开了所有的拘束。

sentences.en: Perhaps you felt moved during an emotional wedding to make a revealing personal speech.
sentences.zh: 也许你在一个感人的婚礼上备受触动，发表了一番袒露心声的个人演讲。

sentences.en: Or maybe you felt your blood pressure rising at a political rally and found yourself sucked
sentences.zh: 或者，你可能在一次政治集会上感到血压上升，发现自己被

sentences.en: in by the mood of the crowd around you.

sentences.en: Meena Chakara is a psychologist at Harvard University.
sentences.zh: 米娜·恰卡拉是哈佛大学的心理学家。

sentences.en: She studies what happens to us in these moments.
sentences.zh: 她研究我们在这些时刻会发生什么变化。

sentences.en: She explores how being part of a group can be powerfully transformative and how we can
sentences.zh: 她探索了成为群体的一部分如何具有强大的变革力量，以及我们如何能够

sentences.en: learn to keep our heads when everyone around us is losing theirs.
sentences.zh: 在周围所有人失去理智时，学会保持冷静。
